question: Why is electronic conductance in AB-stacked bilayer graphene insensitive to the position of monolayer nanoribbon leads?
answer: The electronic conductance in AB-stacked bilayer graphene is insensitive to the position of monolayer nanoribbon leads due to the spatial localization of edge states in the low-energy regime (E < 0.3 eV). These states, primarily confined to AB-stacked regions of the moiré pattern, are decoupled from the lead positions because they reside far from the flake boundaries and contacts. In contrast, higher-energy states (E > 0.3 eV) exhibit lead-dependent conductance due to their delocalized nature across the flake. Thus, the AB-stacked edge states dominate low-energy transport, rendering conductance largely unaffected by lead configuration.

The paper investigates the transport properties of twisted bilayer graphene flakes connected to monolayer nanoribbon leads. The study focuses on understanding the electronic conductance behavior, particularly in the low-energy regime, and how it is influenced by the stacking configuration (AB stacking) and the spatial localization of edge states. The research aims to identify the role of edge states in governing conductance and the relative insensitivity of conductance to lead positions in the case of AB stacking.
